population.span: CONFIRM-HF was a multi-centre, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial that enrolled 304 ambulatory symptomatic HF patients with left ventricular ejection fraction ≤45%, elevated natriuretic peptides, and iron deficiency (ferritin <100 ng/mL or 100–300 ng/mL if transferrin saturation <20%).

endpoint.span: Time to first hospitalization due to worsening heart failure.

estimate.span: Treatment with FCM was associated with a significant reduction in the risk of hospitalization due to worsening HF with a time-to-event analysis returning an HR of 0.39 with a 95% CI of (0.19–0.82)

ci.span: Treatment with FCM was associated with a significant reduction in the risk of hospitalization due to worsening HF with a time-to-event analysis returning an HR of 0.39 with a 95% CI of (0.19–0.82)

analysis_set.span: The time to first hospitalization due to worsening heart failure was estimated using the Kaplan–Meier method, on the full-analysis set.

treatment_strategy.span: Patients were randomized 1 : 1 to treatment with i.v. iron, as ferric carboxymaltose (FCM, n = 152) or placebo (saline, n = 152) for 52 weeks.

follow_up.span: Importantly, patients treated with FCM demonstrated significantly reduced risk of hospital admission due to worsening HF during 1-year follow-up.

served_mismatch: The served HR and CI match the source for first HF hospitalization. However, the estimate uses the full-analysis set (150 FCM, 151 placebo), excluding three randomized patients without post-baseline efficacy assessments; an unqualified all-randomized ITT label is inaccurate. The reported HR also differs from the requested RR estimand and must not be treated as an RR.

candidate_rejections.span: Treatment with FCM was associated with a significant reduction in the risk of hospitalization due to worsening HF with a time-to-event analysis returning an HR of 0.39 with a 95% CI of (0.19–0.82)
candidate_rejections.why: Reject its interpretation as an all-randomized ITT RR; retain the reported first-event HR on the full-analysis set.

entry_population_matches_question.why: Entry criteria specify adults with iron deficiency and stable chronic HF with reduced LVEF; ITT is an analysis-set requirement, addressed separately.
entry_population_matches_question.span: Iron deficient subjects with stable chronic heart failure (CHF) (NYHA II-III) on optimal background therapy for CHF * Reduced left ventricular ejection fraction * Capable of completing 6 minute walk test * At least 18 years of age

notes: Registry evidence confirms adult eligibility. Full text supplies all seven field bindings. Deaths were censored for first HF hospitalization; this is neither the hospitalization/death composite nor the recurrent-event rate ratio. BOUND indicates source binding, not conformity with the requested RR/ITT estimand.
